audits.povRegister: POV CHARACTER: Jaina Proudmoore. REGISTER SUMMARY: Kirin Tor prodigy and Antonidas's apprentice. She thinks faster than she talks and corrects herself mid-thought ('Caution, a good apprentice's caution - oh, Light, no.'), is dry and unfair about herself ('Brilliant, Jaina.'), swears by the Light, and uses technical magic terms (lattice, residue, resonance, drag in the pulse). Her analogies come from the Violet Citadel (benches, first-years, anatomy masters, the quartermaster) and, when tired, from her father's ships (amidships, hold, running rigging). In this chapter she deliberately condescends to 'soldiers'. She would NOT think in essay generalizations, mood labels, or military-analytic summaries. REGISTER CONFIDENCE: HIGH (voice sheet plus a long on-page sample).

audits.cleanReason: I swept every narration sentence against A1-A8 and B1-B4 after writing down Jaina's register. Verdict-tag fragments ('Still right, though.', 'Places, of course.', 'The obvious place to start. A soldier's choice.', 'Short.', 'A fair guess. No.') are her own muttered condescension and self-correction. The plan's arc deliberately has her misread Sylvanas as a blunt soldier until Beat 9, and each one passes the 'could she mutter it?' test. The generalizations ('Any farmwife in Lordaeron', 'Deer ran from horses.', 'A body that had simply died carried its own mark') are working inferences that drive her next conclusion. The only generic-you in narration ('you couldn't ride to everywhere', L191) appears once and is clearly hers. Atmospheric frames (L101 currents after the colon, L380 noise before the doe, L334 cow) either name the source at once or delay it because she really did perceive it that way. The tool-flagged narrator_verdict at L131 ('too smooth for any river') is a concrete physical description locked by Ch1 continuity. The two residual seep candidates were already killed under their child-guide codes.

audits.cleanReason: Candidates were the tool-flagged hedges and vague pointers (L179, L390, L418, L424, L472, L498), the decision fragments that read like note-speak ('The substance, then.', 'Smaller, then.', 'Short.', 'Millhaven, then.'), the stand-in nouns ('answer' L53/L205, 'shape' L35, 'the wrongness' L229/L570, 'the stuff' L496, 'costs' L257/L261, 'things' L504/L512), the tactical summaries (L155, L247, L424, L512) and the dialogue claims (L9, L25-27, L297-299, L514). Every note-speak fragment is followed in the next sentence by its concrete payload: the speech itself, the place/thing/working hypotheses, the cut-down river explanation, the crossroads questions. The stand-in nouns are anchored by local sensory carriers (coin taste, late drag, the circled stones, the cracked-crucible comparison). 'The wrongness' is Jaina's in-world name for the unnamed contamination, so the subject-matter defense applies. 'Something in there' (L472) compresses only after the heat has been shown, and the next sentences go and find it. The tactical reads (L424 calls, L512 'not one of them had said hurry') follow visible route and position evidence (L247, L510). No line needed offstage knowledge to cash out.

There are three translation setups. (1) L23 'The short version; a soldier would want it short.' leads to L25-27. (2) L267 'built the explanation ... cutting it down. Short.' leads to the L275 river analogy. (3) L466 'Tell me what's in her.' leads to L514. In (1) and (2) the simplification fails on purpose, and the prose says so in so many words (L35 'She had cut out the lattice ... left what any village wisewoman might say'; L285 'A river over its banks. Damp up a wick ... Rot in a cellar.'). Windrunner's follow-ups ('Which stones read worst. Where.' / 'Your lines don't spread') are the scene's built-in 'which one?' that exposes the thinness, matching plan Beats 2 and 8-9 ('exposed by her own simplification'; 'misreads her audience again'). Killing these would erase the arc. (3) is a working plain answer with usable targets (blood, meat, liver worst, lungs, alive before the arrow). Windrunner's next question ('Is it in my horses?') opens a new line of enquiry, not a request to unpack the answer.
